description: You can search the web for current events, office holders, election results, and anything that may have changed, including release dates, casts, prices and news; read the top pages.
author: MaiPai

examples: search the web for the tallest mountain
search online for tonight's game score
search the web for the weather forecast
search the web for the closest pharmacy
what's the latest book by my favorite author
when does the new season come out
is the hardware store open right now
what's the current price of that
has there been any news about that lately

expression.description: The search words, a short plain query about what the person asked. A follow-up like "is he in it" is about the previous message's subject: search for that subject.

category.description: Leave this out. A search is a general web search by default. Set it to images only when the person asks to see pictures or photos; a question about a date, a fact, a price, the news or a person is never an image search.

read_page.description: Leave this out. Home reads the top result pages itself on every search.

data_sources.what: the search query, nothing else; an image search is the same query to the same instance, with the images category
data_sources.who: whichever search engines the household's own SearXNG instance is configured to use
data_sources.retention: controlled entirely by the household's own SearXNG instance

data_sources.destination: the first few pages of a search's results, and the page URL named by the household's request
data_sources.when: a search finds results (Home reads up to three of the result pages), or the household asks what a page says or asks for a link, price, fix, download, or driver on that page
data_sources.what: an ordinary page request for each page URL, nothing about the household or the question

data_sources.when: web search is set up and either your SearXNG instance is down or a search comes back with nothing - on by default, turn it off under web search settings
data_sources.retention: controlled entirely by the Wikimedia Foundation; see their own privacy policy
